caveats: Coverage layer, not an individual-building count. Tightly clustered houses merge into single footprints because of imagery resolution. Use OSM or Overture (on hot_flood_npl) for exact totals.
methodology_other: AI building detection on ESRI World Imagery, edge-regularised.
name: hot_flood_npl_buildings_fair
notes:
AI-detected building coverage and H3 density grid for the 132.93 km² 1 km riparian buffer along the Upper Trishuli and Bhote Koshi rivers, published for the 2026 flash flood response.

This layer is meant to show **where structures are**, not to count individual buildings. Because imagery resolution is limited, tightly clustered houses are often merged into a single footprint, so counts under-report the true number. Use [hot_flood_npl](https://data.humdata.org/dataset/hot_flood_npl) (OpenStreetMap and Overture) for accurate per-building totals.

- Estimated ~13,663 building coverage footprints across the corridor
- H3 res 10 density grid (~0.015 km² per cell), block-scale detail
- Interactive report with map and cross-reference to OSM and Overture

**Caveats.** Small stone-and-tile houses common in Rasuwa hillside settlements are often merged or missed. Post-event damage is not published here.
